title: Relative risk as a named ratio of probabilities
dek: RR = π1/π0. Wikipedia contrast. Collapses toward 1 as baselines rise even when OR stays put.
story: Relative risk on Wikipedia is a ratio of two probabilities, the contrast people think they heard when they heard 'twice as likely'. Log-binomial models and some Poisson-with-robust-SE tricks estimate it directly; logits do not.
Case-control studies generally do not identify RR without extra information; they do better at OR. That is why the logit celebrity exists.
Incidence ratios with person-time are a neighbouring object (stats-incidence-prevalence).
deep: Cohort/trial with counted events and a defined denominator: RR is on the table.
Log link + binomial can wander above 1; that is why people use constraints or Poisson tricks.
Do not convert OR to RR with a bogus formula you found under a Wikipedia talk page without stating π0.
Risk difference is a third contrast (absolute), often more decision-relevant.

visual.caption: Design first, then which contrast is identified. Case-control points at OR, not at RR, unless extra assumptions enter.
